what: Sev0 on the owner's call at 01:23 Pacific: pull requests were not landing, and many were open and conflicting. Most red runs were on laws the change never touched: the L11 storage law at its 60 s limit (9 red and 5 green on PR and queue runs that night), the watcher laws L17 and L18, the tezgah fold L33 hang (ticket 1166) and the L15 gateway wake (ticket 1163). The next job itself failed 0 times in 24 hours (188 ready runs measured); the reds came from the related job's integration legs and the next job's e2e legs. Twenty fixes landed one at a time. The sev0 closed at 12:25 Pacific, by the lead, with nothing left open, and a sev1 followed at once (issue 1631, one scheduled law red on main from before the fixes).
cause: Integration and visual laws that need a real resource ran on every pull request and queue run, so their flakes blocked unrelated changes, and conflicts piled up while nothing landed. Admin merges were refused from 02:00 to 03:50, the queue built two entries at once, and the kalfa stack could not land whole.
fix: Integration and visual laws left pull requests and the merge queue (0602; 1613, 1615, 1618): main's full run carries them. Stacks are gone (0603, 1625): each layer lands on its own, and in a sev0 the lead admin-merges each ready pull request in order, while out of a sev0 the merge queue stays the normal route. Each flake got its own fix: 1616 (L11), 1542 and 1639 (watcher L17, L18 and L10), 1612 (L33), 1620 (L15), 1622 (L13 guard), 1624 (P8 kill race).
test: Main's full run is the net for the laws that left the merge line; its first red is the measure. Ticket 1173 makes lint fail a tracked *.rej or *.orig.

after: Still open at the close: none. Flake tickets found while fixing, each with an owner: 1168 and 1169 (L13), 1170 (P8 kill race), 1172 (L10), 1174 (watcher laws' heap), 1175 (L10 misses a dead stream), 1176 (the watcher file's other clock waits); 1171 is the product half of the L11 fix, and 1173 catches a tracked patch reject.
cost: The freeze canceled 62 runs on 7 branches, and 1,522 GitHub calls failed, most of them the sev loop's retries before 1617 (the REST limit reached 0 of 5,000 at 02:01). From 02:00 to 03:50 nothing landed. Thirteen queue fixes took about six hours. Runner minutes and agent dollars were not recorded during the sev, so neither is here.
learned: A law that needs a real resource does not belong on the merge line. This matches Google's split: presubmit runs the small and medium tests a change reaches, and a continuous post-submit run carries the large ones (Software Engineering at Google, chapter 23).
The template copy alone gave L11 only 1 to 2 s on CI; splitting the law into 16 parts gave room, with the slowest part at 12.5 to 15 s of its 60 s.
Git 2.56 on CI deepens a shallow clone differently from 2.40 on the laptop, so a leakgrep law was green locally and red on CI; only CI guards those lines.

The freeze canceled main's own check runs, so a red main (1517 left scripts/typecheck.sh on NOT_YET_PORTED after 1506 deleted it) went unseen until pull requests merging main turned red. The sev skill should allow main by default in a sev0.
A patch reject reached main: 1032 landed a .rej in place of its test hunks, and lint, CI and the admin merge all passed it. 1504's review found it.
The sev loop's retries on runs GitHub will not cancel (HTTP 409) emptied the REST limit. Earlier in the night the lead called those lines harmless, which was wrong.
Reviews found real faults in every CI fix but one, and each landed after one fix round, two at most (0564 for 1617 and 1621).
unknown: This note cannot tell whether moving integration laws off pull requests lets a real break reach main that a pull request run would have caught; main's full run is the net, and its first red will tell. It cannot give runner minutes or agent dollars, which nothing recorded. The L11 split's 10 repeat runs were on a cloud box, and the owner has not said whether cloud-box proofs count.
